comparison: Perfect overlap on myosin dynamics claims (C40-C51). OpenEval finds comprehensive quantitative imaging data fully supports position-dependent activation model. Peer reviewers accept the observations but request methodological clarifications without challenging the findings themselves.

Perfect overlap on overexpression experiments (C127-C131). OpenEval finds phenotypes support the regulatory hierarchy. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, requiring distinction between excessive contractility effects versus domain expansion effects, and questioning whether Fog expression levels are comparable to endogenous.

Perfect overlap on geometric constraint model (C132-C135). Both evaluations support the theoretical framework and its experimental validation. Peer reviewer only requests methodological clarification about sample sizes without challenging the result.

High overlap on Fkh/Hkb independence claims (C120-C124, C144-C146). OpenEval finds the inference reasonable given mutant data. Peer Reviewer #2 expresses confusion about how unchanged Fkh pattern explains the hkb mutant delay, indicating the logic is unclear or insufficiently supported.

High overlap on transcription factor dynamics and timing (C89-C105). OpenEval finds live-imaging data with temporal correlations support the model and are consistent with gene expression kinetics. Peer reviewers request more detailed discussion of timing to confirm events are consistent with the proposed mechanism.

Substantial overlap on cell tracking and position-dependent behavior (C32-C38). OpenEval finds quantitative cell tracking data from multiple time points converge to support dynamic patterning. Peer Reviewer #1 explicitly requests cell tracking visualization to unambiguously demonstrate cells move and change shape, indicating current evidence is insufficient.

Moderate overlap on overarching mechanistic model (C3-C7, C27, C141-C142). OpenEval finds the model well-supported by convergence of multiple data types. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, with Essential Revision #1 requiring experiments altering expression patterns rather than complete loss-of-function, and multiple reviewers questioning timing and specificity.

Moderate overlap on hkb mutant phenotype characterization (C52-C64 and related claims). OpenEval finds comprehensive quantitative analysis provides strong evidence for position-dependent behavior specification. Peer reviewers accept the detailed observations but note limitations in interpretation, as complete transcription factor loss affects many processes beyond the proposed specific pathway.

Moderate overlap on Fog localization and correlation with constriction (C111-C114). OpenEval finds correlation between Fog levels and both apical area reduction and myosin intensity strengthens mechanistic link. Peer Reviewer #3 questions causality, noting apical constriction might concentrate apically secreted Fog rather than Fog causing constriction, requesting temporal precedence analysis.

Moderate overlap on basic morphological observations (C8-C12, C20-C22). Both evaluations support these foundational observations about asymmetric geometry and spatial organization. These establish the study's motivation and are not questioned by either evaluation.

Moderate overlap on strain rate decomposition and cell shape analysis (C65-C74, C81-C82). OpenEval finds the quantitative measurements methodologically sound and support disrupted patterning conclusion. Peer reviewers accept findings but note presentation complexity makes it difficult to follow, requesting simplification without rejecting results.

Overlap on upstream regulators and speculative claims (C148-C150). OpenEval rates as uncertain due to 'data not shown' and explicit speculation. Peer reviewers accept these as contextual observations from previous work without questioning them.

Overlap on comparative mechanisms and general principles (C160-C162). OpenEval finds synthesis appropriately qualified with reasonable speculation. Peer reviewers accept these discussion points as important context for interpreting findings.

Overlap on background and established knowledge claims (C13-C19 and others). Both evaluations support these contextual claims citing prior work. These provide appropriate background without being novel findings.

Partial overlap on temporal inference claims (C103-C105). OpenEval finds inferences reasonable based on temporal correlations and known kinetics, though notes direct demonstration would strengthen conclusions. Peer reviewers request more detailed timing discussion to confirm consistency with the model.
Partial overlap on Fog expression in fkh mutants (C118-C119). Both evaluations support these observations about the regulatory relationship between Fkh and Fog without questioning the findings.

Partial overlap on cell elongation and intercalation analysis (C81-C82). OpenEval finds data support conclusion that hkb mutant intercalations lack wild-type signatures. Peer reviewers accept findings but note presentation complexity.

Partial overlap on junctional myosin polarity (C79-C80). OpenEval finds measurements methodologically sound. Peer reviewers accept observations but request clarification of y-axis definition without questioning findings.
Partial overlap on Hkb/Fkh regulatory independence (C124). Both evaluations support this observation about independent regulation of the two transcription factors.

Partial overlap on Fog and transcriptional regulation (C24, C126). OpenEval finds Fog localization data with mutant analysis demonstrates Hkb and Fkh dependence. Peer Reviewer #3 questions whether loss-of-function evidence alone is sufficient for specific regulatory claims, requiring pattern-altering experiments.

Partial overlap on mechanistic model components (C125, C138-C140, C147). OpenEval finds convergence of evidence supports the model. Peer reviewers require additional experiments beyond complete transcription factor loss to support specific regulatory claims.

Minimal overlap on general principles (C5). OpenEval finds these appropriately qualified. Peer reviewers question whether pit position versus size effects can be distinguished in overexpression experiments.

Minimal overlap on computational predictions and published data examination (C155-C156). OpenEval rates as uncertain due to lack of experimental validation. Peer reviewers accept these as contextual discussion points.

Minimal overlap on late-stage hkb phenotypes (C136). OpenEval finds imaging data supports phenotype characterization. Peer reviewers accept observations but note interpretation limitations regarding specificity.
Minimal overlap on contextual claims from cited work (C158). Both evaluations support these as appropriate inferences from literature providing context.
